features.title: One picture to a 3D Gaussian splat
features.what: A render, a generated image or a photo becomes a 3D Gaussian splat.
features.evidence_quote: Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat.

features.title: Even the hidden sides
features.what: Up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, including sides the picture never showed.
features.evidence_quote: generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, written as a standard 3DGS `.ply`

features.title: Background cut, object framed
features.what: The pipeline isolates the object before reconstructing it.
features.evidence_quote: it removes the background, frames the object

features.title: Runs on consumer GPUs
features.what: 7.2 GB of VRAM; can run in under 2 seconds.
features.evidence_quote: It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.

features.title: Standard .ply out
features.what: The file opens in any Gaussian-splat viewer or Blender.

features.title: Free Space demo + open SDK
features.what: A Hugging Face Space demo, and `pip install -e .` for the SDK with one Python call.

features.title: Photo mode and render mode
features.what: `--mode real` for photographs, `--mode synthetic` for renders of a single object.

features.title: Benchmark edges TripoSplat and TRELLIS
features.what: Bold in SSIM, LPIPS, IoU, DINOv2, CLIP and sharpness distance on the lab's table.
features.evidence_quote: TripoSplat and TRELLIS lose every visual column

features.title: Exact command you can copy
features.what: One line turns a photo into a .ply on your own machine.

features.title: Two encoders are gated
features.what: Accept terms once on DINOv3 and FLUXXX.2 before the SDK will run.
features.evidence_quote: it reads input through two gated models

risks.text: Your own runs need an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA (the free Space demo needs no GPU).
Built for single objects — it frames one object per picture, not scenes.
